questions.question: The Green Revolution was instrumental in reducing India's dependence on imports of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Food grains**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Green Revolution was primarily aimed at increasing agricultural production in India.
 
• It led to a significant increase in the production of **food grains** such as wheat and rice.
 
• This increase in domestic production helped reduce India's dependence on imports of **food grains**.
 
• The Green Revolution introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• It played a crucial role in transforming India from a food-deficient to a food-surplus country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution in India began in the 1960s and was largely funded by international agencies.
 
• It was initially implemented in the states of Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Norman Borlaug, an American agronomist, is often called the father of the Green Revolution for his work in developing high-yielding crop varieties.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution in India is attributed to the collaborative efforts of scientists, policymakers, and farmers.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Depreciation?

I. Depreciation is termed as loss of value of fixed assets due to wear and tear during its useful life.

II. Depreciation does not take into account unexpected or sudden destruction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) Both I and II**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Depreciation** is defined as the loss of value of fixed assets due to wear and tear during its useful life. This is a systematic allocation of the cost of an asset over its useful life. ***Hence, Statement I is correct.***
 
• Depreciation calculations typically do not take into account unexpected or sudden destruction of assets, such as those caused by natural disasters or accidents. These events are usually covered under different accounting treatments like impairment or loss. ***Hence, Statement II is correct.***
 
• Depreciation is used to allocate the cost of tangible assets over their useful lives, reflecting their consumption, wear and tear, or obsolescence.
 
• It helps in matching the cost of the asset with the revenue it generates, following the matching principle in accounting.
 
• Methods of depreciation include straight-line, declining balance, and units of production, among others, each having its own application depending on the nature of the asset and its usage.

questions.question: Constitutions limit the power of government in many ways. The most common way of limiting the power of government is to specify certain _______ that all of us possess as citizens and which no government can ever be allowed to violate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are the basic human rights enshrined in the Constitution of India which are guaranteed to all citizens.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the holistic development of individuals and the preservation of human dignity.
 
• The Constitution of India provides six fundamental rights to its citizens:
 
 
• Right to Equality
 
• Right to Freedom
 
• Right Against Exploitation
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies
 
 
 
• Fundamental Rights act as limitations on the powers of the government, ensuring that the state does not encroach upon the basic liberties of individuals.
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning that any violation can be challenged in a court of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• **Economic Duties** and **Fundamental Duties** refer to the responsibilities of citizens towards the state and society, but they do not limit the powers of the government.
 
• The **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• The protection of these rights is essential for the functioning of a democratic society and the assurance of justice, equality, and liberty to all citizens.

questions.question: In Olympics table tennis event, if the points are tied at 10-10, a player then has to strive for a _________ point lead to win the game.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **2 points lead** is required to win the game when the points are tied at 10-10 in an Olympics table tennis event.
 
• This rule ensures a clear margin of victory, preventing a win by a narrow margin of just one point.
 
• The rule applies to both singles and doubles matches in table tennis.
 
• Players alternate serves after each point once the score reaches 10-10, increasing the intensity and fairness of the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Table tennis** is governed by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), which sets the rules for international competitions.
 
• The game is played with a small, lightweight ball and paddles, on a hard table divided by a net.
 
• Table tennis became an Olympic sport in 1988, with singles and doubles events for both men and women.
 
• The sport is known for its fast pace and requires quick reflexes and strategic play.
 
• Matches are typically played to the best of five or seven games, with each game won by the first player to reach 11 points, provided there is a two-point margin.

questions.question: In August 2023, the Central government has granted a _________ extension to Cabinet Secretary Rajiv Gauba, making him the longest-serving cabinet secretary in India's history.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In August 2023, the Central government has granted a **one-year** extension to Cabinet Secretary Rajiv Gauba.
 
• This extension makes Rajiv Gauba the **longest-serving cabinet secretary** in India's history.
 
• Cabinet Secretaries in India typically serve a fixed term, but extensions can be granted based on the government's discretion.
 
• Rajiv Gauba's extension reflects his significant contributions and the trust the government places in his leadership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The position of the **Cabinet Secretary** is the top-most executive official and senior-most civil servant of the Government of India.
 
• The Cabinet Secretary is the ex-officio head of the Civil Services Board, the Cabinet Secretariat, the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), and all civil services under the rules of business of the government.
 
• The role of the Cabinet Secretary is to provide assistance to the Council of Ministers and act as the chief coordinator of the central government.
 
• Rajiv Gauba, an IAS officer of the 1982 batch, has held various significant positions in the government before becoming the Cabinet Secretary.
